Class StatementDecoratorInterceptor

java.lang.Object
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.JdbcInterceptor
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.StatementDecoratorInterceptor
All Implemented Interfaces:
InvocationHandler
Direct Known Subclasses:
StatementCache
public class StatementDecoratorInterceptor extends AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor
Implementation of JdbcInterceptor that proxies statements and result sets so that neither the physical session nor the driver's own handles reach the application through them: Statement.getConnection() is answered with the pool's connection handle rather than the driver's connection, and ResultSet.getStatement() with the statement handle rather than the driver's statement - the hiding of the physical connection this interceptor exists for (Bug 48392, described in this interceptor's section of the jdbc-pool documentation page).

Beyond the hiding, the statement proxy keeps its own handle contract: calls reach the driver statement only while the proxy is open, a repeat close answers as a no-op, every other call on a retired handle is refused with an SQLException, and the driver's answer to a close that failed is passed to the caller - the handle is retired whichever way the driver answered. The connection the proxy reports is a snapshot of the borrow that created it, so a component that reuses a statement across borrows - StatementCache - must re-bind the handle first, as StatementDecoratorInterceptor.StatementProxy.setConnection(Object) documents. The result set proxy answers ResultSet.getStatement() and the Object identity methods (toString, equals, hashCode) itself; every other call, the Wrapper methods included, reaches the driver object unchanged.

  • Method Details

    • closeInvoked

      public void closeInvoked()
      Description copied from class: AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor
      Method invoked when the operation Connection.close() is invoked. It runs before the close is passed down the chain, so that a hook can still reach the connection while it is alive - statements must be closed before the session is handed to the next borrower. Implementation of this method should be thought through with care, as no actions should trigger an exception. An interceptor that nevertheless throws is isolated: the exception is logged and ignored, the remaining interceptors in the chain still receive the close, and the connection is returned to the pool as it would have been. The fatal virtual machine errors the pool never swallows are the exception: those propagate.
      Specified by:
      closeInvoked in class AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor

    • createStatement

      public Object createStatement(Object proxy, Method method, Object[] args, Object statement, long time)
      Wraps the statement the connection call has just created in this interceptor's proxy. This method will be invoked after a successful statement creation. This method can choose to return a wrapper around the statement or return the statement itself. If this method returns a wrapper then it should return a wrapper object that implements one of the following interfaces. Statement, PreparedStatement or CallableStatement

      An implementation must not make the statement reachable from any other code before it returns, because if this method throws then the statement is closed on a best-effort basis by the interceptor base class before the throwable is propagated to the application.

      The time argument is unused - this interceptor does no timing. If building the proxy fails, the failure is logged and the unproxied driver statement is returned, so a failure degrades the connection hiding rather than failing the application's call.

      Specified by:
      createStatement in class AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor
      Parameters:
      proxy - the actual proxy object
      method - the method that was called. It will be one of the methods defined in AbstractCreateStatementInterceptor.STATEMENT_TYPES
      args - the arguments to the method
      statement - the statement that the underlying connection created
      time - elapsed time in milliseconds, measured with the monotonic clock
      Returns:
      a Statement object
